sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些举足轻重的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话实时发生。

sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不会想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The CEOs of the nation's most influential technology companies, Amazon, Apple, Google, and Facebook, are brought before Congress to answer a question.
sentences.zh: 国家最具影响力的科技公司——亚马逊、苹果、谷歌和脸书的首席执行官们被传唤到国会回答一个问题。

sentences.en: Are they the two powerful and two dominant monopolies of the internet age?
sentences.zh: 它们是否是互联网时代两个强大且占据统治地位的垄断企业？

sentences.en: My colleague, Cecilia Kang, was in the room.
sentences.zh: 我的同事塞西莉亚·康当时就在现场。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: Cecilia, we are talking just ahead of the start of what is probably the most anticipated hearing in the history of the tech industry.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉亚，我们正值科技史上最受期待的听证会开幕前夕进行交谈。

sentences.en: So just to begin, why is this hearing happening at all?
sentences.zh: 那么首先，这场听证会究竟为什么要召开？

sentences.en: This hearing is happening because there is a recognition across government that these four very powerful and very important companies to the economy have become so dominant
sentences.zh: 这场听证会的召开是因为政府上下普遍认识到，这四家对经济非常强大且非常重要的公司已经变得如此具有统治地位

sentences.en: that they are harming consumers and harming competition.
sentences.zh: 以至于它们正在损害消费者和竞争。

sentences.en: So Congress has summoned the CEOs of the corporations, Jeff Bezos of Amazon, Tim Cook of Apple, Mark Zuckerberg of Facebook,
sentences.zh: 因此，国会传唤了这些公司的首席执行官，亚马逊的杰夫·贝佐斯、苹果的蒂姆·库克、脸书的马克·扎克伯格

sentences.en: and Sundar Pichai of Google to ask them and interrogate them on their business practices and find out if
sentences.zh: 以及谷歌的桑达尔·皮查伊，就他们的商业做法对他们进行质问和盘问，并查明

sentences.en: these internet giants that have become, in many ways, the new trusts of our economy, if they are harming consumers and competition.
sentences.zh: 这些在许多方面已成为我们经济中新托拉斯的互联网巨头，是否在损害消费者和竞争。

sentences.en: So how exactly do we get to this point where these four executives are being summoned before Congress and being forced to confront that question?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们究竟是如何走到这一步，让这四位高管被传唤到国会并被迫直面这个问题的？

sentences.en: I think you can start with the 2016 presidential election that really was a wake-up call in
sentences.zh: 我想你可以从2016年总统大选开始说起，那确实给华盛顿

sentences.en: Washington and across the world, really, about the power of these social media platforms to be used for harm, not just for entertainment and good.
sentences.zh: 乃至全世界敲响了警钟，让人意识到这些社交媒体平台的力量会被用于作恶，而不仅仅是娱乐和好事。

sentences.en: The presidential election of 2020 in the United States then really picked up on this feeling of concern.
sentences.zh: 随后，美国2020年总统大选真正加剧了这种担忧情绪。

sentences.en: I'm deeply concerned right now that the space around companies like Amazon, Facebook, Google is now referred to by venture capitalists as the kill zone.
sentences.zh: 我现在深感担忧的是，亚马逊、脸书、谷歌等公司周围的空间现在被风险投资家称为“杀戮地带”。

sentences.en: And we saw for the first time a political candidate, Elizabeth Warren, announced her promise to break up big tech.
sentences.zh: 我们第一次看到一位政治候选人伊丽莎白·沃伦宣布承诺拆分大型科技公司。

sentences.en: Break those things apart and we will have a much more competitive, robust market in America.
sentences.zh: 把这些东西拆开，我们在美国就会拥有一个更具竞争力的、更有活力的市场。

sentences.en: That's how capitalism should work.
sentences.zh: 这才是资本主义应有的运作方式。

sentences.en: This was the first time that even the real term, big tech, became sort of part of our lexicon.
sentences.zh: 这是“大型科技公司”这个真正的词汇第一次真正成为我们词汇的一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And almost like a kind of epithet.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎带有一种贬义色彩。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: You have criticized a lot of big banks.
sentences.zh: 你批评过很多大银行。

sentences.en: Today you're talking about breaking up big tech.
sentences.zh: 今天你在谈论拆分大型科技公司。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: So here's the deal.
sentences.zh: 所以情况是这样的。

sentences.en: We need real competition in this field.
sentences.zh: 我们这个领域需要真正的竞争。

sentences.en: And there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 而这里有一个问题。

sentences.en: And there was a domino effect after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后产生了多米诺骨牌效应。

sentences.en: So I think that Google and Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谷歌、推特和脸书。

sentences.en: Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: They're really treading on very, very troubled territory and they have to be careful.
sentences.zh: 他们真的是在踩非常非常危险的领地，他们必须小心。

sentences.en: It's not fair to large portions of the population.
sentences.zh: 这对广大民众来说是不公平的。

sentences.en: I'm also really disappointed in a lot of the tech companies.
sentences.zh: 我对很多科技公司也真的很失望。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton, Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿，伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: I think we need vigorous antitrust legislation in this country.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们这个国家需要强有力的反垄断立法。

sentences.en: All articulated similar concerns about big tech.
sentences.zh: 所有人都表达了对大型科技公司的类似担忧。

sentences.en: They have incredible power over the economy, over the political life of this country in a very dangerous sense.
sentences.zh: 它们对经济、对这个国家的政治生活拥有令人难以置信的权力，从某种非常危险的意义上说。

sentences.en: Soon after, the ground moved underneath the technology companies in Washington.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，华盛顿科技公司的基础发生了动摇。

sentences.en: In the span of one week in June 2019, the Department of Justice, the Federal Trade Commission
sentences.zh: 在2019年6月的一周时间内，司法部、联邦贸易委员会

sentences.en: and state attorneys generals all announced that they had opened investigations into the biggest technology companies.
sentences.zh: 和各州总检察长全都宣布对最大的科技公司展开调查。

sentences.en: It was unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 这是前所未有的。

sentences.en: These companies have not been investigated except for
sentences.zh: 在美国，除了

sentences.en: Google on antitrust grounds before in the United States.
sentences.zh: 谷歌曾因反垄断理由被调查外，这些公司从未受过调查。

sentences.en: And beyond that, it was a real recognition to put these four companies into a cohort.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，这也是将这四家公司归为一类的重要共识。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can briefly walk us through how each of these companies' behavior has gotten them to this point, to this hearing room.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否简要地向我们介绍一下，这四家公司各自的行为是如何把它们带到这一步、带到这个听证室的。

sentences.en: Because these four companies are all big and they're all tech, but they're actually all pretty different, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这四家公司体量都很大，而且都是科技公司，但它们实际上截然不同，对吧？

sentences.en: So what exactly has each done that people during this hearing are going to be confronting them about?
sentences.zh: 那么，它们各自到底做了什么，让这场听证会的人们要质问它们？

sentences.en: So in the case of Amazon, the accusation is that it is both a retailer and it is a platform for third-party sellers.
sentences.zh: 所以在亚马逊的案子中，指控它是零售商，同时也是第三方卖家的平台。

sentences.en: In other words, you know, another small business that might sell, let's say, a face mask or tissue paper that will sell their goods on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道，另一个小企业可能出售，比方说，口罩或纸巾，它们会在亚马逊上出售商品。

sentences.en: And the accusation is that Amazon abuses its position and its clout to make sure that their own products will always perform better than these third parties.
sentences.zh: 而指控是亚马逊滥用其地位和影响力，确保它们自己的产品表现总是优于这些第三方。

sentences.en: And they also use the data and the intelligence they have to suppress and to charge these third-party sellers more.
sentences.zh: 它们还利用拥有的数据和情报来压制并向这些第三方卖家收取更多费用。

sentences.en: In the case of Apple, the accusation is that it unfairly uses its clout over the app store.
sentences.zh: 在苹果的案子中，指控是它不公平地利用了对应用商店的影响力。

sentences.en: I mean, the app store is huge.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，应用商店太庞大了。

sentences.en: It has more than a million apps on it and it uses its power over the platform to block rivals and to force the apps that are on the app store to pay high commissions.
sentences.zh: 上面有超过一百万个应用程序，它利用对平台权力来阻止竞争对手，并强迫应用商店上的应用程序支付高额佣金。

sentences.en: In the case of Facebook, the accusation is that it is a monopoly in social networking and that it has acquired rivals like Instagram and WhatsApp to maintain its monopoly
sentences.zh: 在脸书的案子中，指控是它是社交网络领域的垄断者，并且它收购了像 Instagram 和 WhatsApp 这样的竞争对手来维持其垄断地位

sentences.en: and in the process really killed off competition on the internet.
sentences.zh: 并在这一过程中彻底扼杀了互联网上的竞争。

sentences.en: In the case of Google, the accusation is that it uses its dominant position in search and online advertising and in the Android smartphone
sentences.zh: 在谷歌的案子中，指控是它利用在搜索、在线广告以及安卓智能手机

sentences.en: market to crush rivals and to continue to maintain its dominance in all of those marketplaces.
sentences.zh: 市场上的统治地位来打压竞争对手，并继续维持其在所有这些市场中的统治地位。

sentences.en: So the common theme here is size, dominance, and basically monopolistic conduct.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的共同主题是规模、统治地位以及基本上属于垄断性质的行为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I would say that they are different companies and they do have different business models.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说，它们是不同的公司，它们确实有不同的商业模式。

sentences.en: But the one thing I would say they have in common is that they are gatekeepers.
sentences.zh: 但我要说它们的共同点是，它们都是守门人。

sentences.en: They are actually like choke points on the internet because they control commerce and they control communications and they control the discovery of information on the internet.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上就像互联网上的咽喉要道，因为它们控制着商业、控制着通信，还控制着互联网上信息的发现。

sentences.en: These are sort of unprecedented in their scope.
sentences.zh: 这些在规模上可以说是前所未有的。

sentences.en: And they're global.
sentences.zh: 而且它们是全球性的。

sentences.en: Everyone around the world uses them.
sentences.zh: 全世界每个人都在使用它们。

sentences.en: So listening to you talk about this hearing, the stakes of it, the questions around influence and conduct, I am inevitably reminded of...
sentences.zh: 所以听你谈论这场听证会、它的利害关系、关于影响力和行为的问题，我不禁让我想起了……

sentences.en: I'd like to ask our guests to please take your seats.
sentences.zh: 我想请各位嘉宾请就座。

sentences.en: What was probably the most famous congressional hearing of my lifetime, which was the tobacco industry hearings of 1994.
sentences.zh: 这大概是我一生中最著名的国会听证会，也就是1994年的烟草行业听证会。

sentences.en: For the first time ever, the chief executive officers of our nation's tobacco companies are testifying together before the United States Congress.
sentences.zh: 美国烟草公司的首席执行官们有史以来第一次一同在美国国会作证。

sentences.en: And of course, tobacco, smoking, health are different than technology.
sentences.zh: 当然，烟草、吸烟、健康与科技不同。

sentences.en: But it was a moment when the top executives of billion-dollar companies and very powerful companies in the economy...
sentences.zh: 但这是一个时刻，价值数十亿美元的公司和经济中极具权力的公司的高管们……

sentences.en: The truth is that cigarettes are the single most dangerous consumer product ever sold.
sentences.zh: 事实是，香烟是有史以来最危险的单一消费品。

sentences.en: ...were summoned before Congress and really held to account in a highly public way.
sentences.zh: ……被传唤到国会，并以高度公开的方式真正被追究责任。

sentences.en: I similarly see the comparison to the tobacco hearings.
sentences.zh: 我同样看到了与烟草听证会的相似之处。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the moment when you have the heads, the captains of the biggest companies in technology, just like we saw the heads, the captains of the biggest companies
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个时刻，科技界最大公司的掌门人、领头羊，正如我们看到烟草行业最大公司的掌门人、领头羊一样

sentences.en: of the tobacco industry, have to come before Congress...
sentences.zh: 不得不来到国会面前……

sentences.en: If you raise your right hand...
sentences.zh: 如果你举起右手……

sentences.en: Stand up...
sentences.zh: 起立……

sentences.en: Do you swear...
sentences.zh: 你们是否发誓……

sentences.en: Raise their right hand, swear in...
sentences.zh: 举起右手，宣誓……

sentences.en: ...the whole truth and nothing but the truth.
sentences.zh: ……说全部真话，毫无虚假。

sentences.en: ...and really...
sentences.zh: ……并且真正……

sentences.en: ...defend themselves as companies that are potentially harmful to society.
sentences.zh: ……为自己作为可能对社会有害的公司的身份进行辩护。

sentences.en: First, I'd like to just go down the row, yes or no.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想挨个问，回答是或否。

sentences.en: Do you believe nicotine is not addictive?
sentences.zh: 你认为尼古丁不上瘾吗？

sentences.en: I believe nicotine is not addictive, yes.
sentences.zh: 我认为尼古丁不上瘾，是的。

sentences.en: Mr. Johnston.
sentences.zh: 约翰斯顿先生。

sentences.en: Congressman, cigarettes and nicotine clearly do not meet the classic definitions of addiction.
sentences.zh: 议员先生，香烟和尼古丁显然不符合成瘾的经典定义。

sentences.en: There is no intoxication.
sentences.zh: 这里没有醉酒状态。

sentences.en: We'll take that as a no.
sentences.zh: 我们就当这是个否定回答。

sentences.en: The moment of reckoning is similar for the tech industry in the way that that was a moment of reckoning for the tobacco industry.
sentences.zh: 对科技行业而言，清算的时刻与当年烟草行业清算的时刻相似。

sentences.en: And of course, in that case, those tobacco hearings, they were the beginning of very serious changes in how the United States regulated tobacco companies.
sentences.zh: 当然，在那次事件中，那些烟草听证会是美国监管烟草公司方式发生重大变革的开端。

sentences.en: There were big reforMs. There were big fines.
sentences.zh: 进行了重大改革。开出了巨额罚单。

sentences.en: It was a turning point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个转折点。

sentences.en: And if this hearing ends up feeling like a turning point for the technology industry, I wonder what the basis for whatever regulation flows from this would be.
sentences.zh: 如果这次听证会最终感觉像是科技行业的转折点，我想知道由此产生的所有监管的基础会是什么。

sentences.en: The hearing is going to be a real test of whether antitrust laws and competition laws that were first created in 1890 can actually apply to internet companies.
sentences.zh: 这场听证会将是对1890年首次制定的反垄断法和竞争法是否真正适用于互联网公司的一次真正考验。

sentences.en: Where the companies of Silicon Valley are just so different than rail, sugar, steel,
sentences.zh: 硅谷的公司与铁路、糖业、钢铁

sentences.en: the trusts that at that time were the inspiration for trust busters like Theodore Roosevelt and others that were trying to contain the power of the big industrialists at that time.
sentences.zh: 这些托拉斯有着天壤之别，当年的托拉斯启发了西奥多·罗斯福等反托拉斯斗士，他们试图遏制当时大型实业家的权力。

sentences.en: So a lot of the conventional tests that have been used on whether a company has violated antitrust laws may not apply.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多用于判断公司是否违反反垄断法的传统测试可能并不适用。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest tests is this test known as the consumer welfare teSt.
sentences.zh: 其中最大的测试之一就是被称为消费者福利测试的测试。

sentences.en: This is a standard that's been used for about 40 years now and very much permeates antitrust thinking in this country.
sentences.zh: 这是一个已经使用了大约40年的标准，并且在很大程度上渗透了这个国家的反垄断思想。

sentences.en: And that question is, are consumers harmed?
sentences.zh: 而那个问题是，消费者受到损害了吗？

sentences.en: It's really hard to prove harm with a company like Google or Facebook when they can say, well, at the end of the day, our products are free.
sentences.zh: 当谷歌或脸书这样的公司可以说，嗯，归根结底，我们的产品是免费的时，要证明它们造成损害真的很难。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, if you don't like us, we're one click away from an alternative.
sentences.zh: 而且归根结底，如果你不喜欢我们，只需点击一下就能找到替代方案。

sentences.en: Well, this is going to be an interesting hearing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这将是一场有趣的听证会。

sentences.en: It certainly will.
sentences.zh: 当然会的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能得到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，请今天就下载《时报》应用程序并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Cecilia Kahn, and it is noon.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是塞西莉亚·卡恩，现在是中午。

sentences.en: I am in the House Judiciary Committee's hearing room in the Rayburn building.
sentences.zh: 我在雷本大楼众议院司法委员会的听证室里。

sentences.en: Right now we have some lawmakers and many of their A's are shuffling in, all with their face masks on.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有一些议员和他们的许多助理正鱼贯而入，他们都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: And there is in the middle of the room, which would normally be about five rows of chairs very tightly packed together.
sentences.zh: 在房间中央，通常会摆放大约五排紧密排列的椅子。

sentences.en: They're all spread apart, about six feet each.
sentences.zh: 它们现在都隔得很开，每排大约相距六英尺。

sentences.en: It's an odd scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个奇怪的场景。

sentences.en: There's a lot of cleansing of desks and microphones.
sentences.zh: 有很多人在擦拭桌子和麦克风。

sentences.en: We have right now a cleanup crew coming in with their gloves and face masks, cleaning off the microphones with some alcohol.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一支清洁队戴着手套和口罩进来，用一些酒精擦拭麦克风。

sentences.en: And everybody being handed Purell and hand wipes.
sentences.zh: 每个人都分到了净手消毒液和手部湿巾。

sentences.en: So that's the scene a few minutes before we begin.
sentences.zh: 这就是开始前几分钟的场景。

sentences.en: The subcommittee will come to order.
sentences.zh: 小组委员会开会。

sentences.en: So Cecilia, tell us how this hearing starts on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 那么塞西莉亚，给我们讲讲周三的听证会是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: So the hearing started just a little bit late, about one hour late.
sentences.zh: 听证会开始得稍微有点晚，大约晚了一个小时。

sentences.en: And the lawmakers, 15 of them, looked towards the back of the room at a big jumbotron-type screen from their dais.
sentences.zh: 15名议员从他们的席位上望向房间后方一块类似巨型高画质电视屏幕的屏幕。

sentences.en: And they saw the faces of the CEOs, dreamed from the homes and offices of Silicon Valley and presumably Seattle with Jeff Bezos.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了首席执行官们的面孔，这些画面是从硅谷的家中和办公室以及杰夫·贝佐斯的西雅图住所直播过来的。

sentences.en: After Chairman Cicilline gavels in the hearing, he begins to ask the CEOs to introduce themselves.
sentences.zh: 在西西林主席敲槌宣布听证会开始后，他开始请各位首席执行官作自我介绍。

sentences.en: And Cecilia, I found these introductions, these five-minute kind of testimonials, surprisingly personal.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉亚，我发现这些介绍，这种五分钟的陈述，出奇地带有个人色彩。

sentences.en: I think the CEOs really wanted to accomplish a lot in these opening remarks.
sentences.zh: 我认为各位首席执行官在开场白中都真诚地希望能取得丰硕的成果。

sentences.en: Thank you, Chairman Cicilline, ranking member, Sensenbrenner, and members of the subcommittee.
sentences.zh: 谢谢主席西西里尼、资深议员森森布伦特以及小组委员会的各位成员。

sentences.en: I was born into great wealth.
sentences.zh: 我出生于巨大的财富之中。

sentences.en: Not monetary wealth, but instead the wealth of a loving family.
sentences.zh: 不是金钱财富，而是充满爱意的家庭所带来的财富。

sentences.en: You heard Jeff Bezos and Sundar Pichai in particular really emphasize their humble roots.
sentences.zh: 尤其是杰夫·贝佐斯和桑达尔·皮查伊，你们听到了他们极力强调自己卑微的出身。

sentences.en: My mom, Jackie, had me when she was a 17-year-old high school student in Albuquerque.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲杰基生我时，是阿尔伯克基一名17岁的高中生。

sentences.en: Being pregnant in high school was not popular.
sentences.zh: 在高中时期怀孕并不是一件受欢迎的事。

sentences.en: I didn't have much access to a computer growing up in India.
sentences.zh: 我在印度长大时，接触电脑的机会不多。

sentences.en: So you can imagine my amazement when I arrived in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象当我来到美国时内心的震惊。

sentences.en: for graduate school and saw an entire lab of computers to use whenever I wanted.
sentences.zh: 为了读研究生，我看到了一整间电脑实验室，只要我想用随时都能用。

sentences.en: They are known as the richest individuals in the world, and that's certainly the case with Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为世界上最富有的人，杰夫·贝佐斯和马克·扎克伯格显然就是这样。

sentences.en: And I think they wanted to be more relatable.
sentences.zh: 我想他们是想显得更平易近人一些。

sentences.en: Each of these companies wanted to start off right off the bat by explaining how they were scrappy for so long.
sentences.zh: 这些公司都想从一开始就解释他们是如何长期艰苦奋斗的。

sentences.en: And they continue to have that scrappy spirit.
sentences.zh: 而且他们将继续保持这种拼搏的精神。

sentences.en: And then in some cases, they aren't monopolies.
sentences.zh: 而在某些情况下，他们并非垄断企业。

sentences.en: Many of our competitors have hundreds of millions or billions of users.
sentences.zh: 我们的许多竞争对手拥有数亿甚至数十亿用户。

sentences.en: Some are upstarts, but others are gatekeepers with the power to decide if we can even release our apps in their app stores to compete with them.
sentences.zh: 有些是新秀，但另一些则是守门人，有权决定我们是否甚至能在他们的应用商店发布应用来与他们竞争。

sentences.en: And that, in fact, there's competition all over the world.
sentences.zh: 事实上，世界各地都存在竞争。

sentences.en: And history shows that if we don't keep innovating, someone will replace every company here today.
sentences.zh: 历史表明，如果我们停止创新，就会有人取代在座的每一家公司。

sentences.en: And that change can often happen faster than you expect.
sentences.zh: 而且这种变化往往比你预期的还要快。

sentences.en: So they wanted to set a line early on to just dispel the notion that there is a big tech kind of threat right now in our economy,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们很早就划清了界限，以消除我们经济中目前存在大型科技威胁这种观念，

sentences.en: and that they, as individual companies, are part of a very vibrant, competitive marketplace that's changing very quickly.
sentences.zh: 并且他们作为独立公司，是充满活力、竞争激烈且瞬息万变的巨大市场的一部分。

sentences.en: — So then we get to the questions from lawmakers to these four CEOs.
sentences.zh: ——那么接下来是议员向这四位首席执行官提问的环节。

sentences.en: And what do you think characterize those questions overall?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些问题总体上有何特点？

sentences.en: — Well, it was fascinating, Michael.
sentences.zh: ——嗯，这太吸引人了，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The Democrats and Republicans were very much split in their approaches.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人在他们的方法上存在很大分歧。

sentences.en: — So my first question, Mr. Pichai, is why does Google steal content from honest businesses?
sentences.zh: ——那么我的第一个问题，皮查伊先生，为什么谷歌要从诚实的企业那里窃取内容？

sentences.en: — Right off the bat, the Democrats launched into very specific questions about antitrust and the antitrust cases against each of these companies.
sentences.zh: ——一开始，民主党人就直接针对反垄断以及针对这些公司的反垄断案件提出了非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: — Mr. Chairman, with respect, I disagree with that characterization.
sentences.zh: ——主席先生，恕我直言，我不同意这种定性。

sentences.en: — They really used this opportunity to show off the most damning evidence that they had collected over 13 months,
sentences.zh: ——他们确实利用这个机会展示了他们历时13个月收集到的最确凿的证据，

sentences.en: the hundreds of hours of interviews that they've held with employees and rivals.
sentences.zh: 以及他们对员工和竞争对手进行的数百小时的采访。

sentences.en: — Conservatives are consumers, too.
sentences.zh: ——保守派也是消费者。

sentences.en: — The Republicans were very coordinated as well on one particular message.
sentences.zh: ——共和党人在一个特定的信息上也高度协同。

sentences.en: — Censorship of conservative viewpoints.
sentences.zh: ——对保守派观点的审查。

sentences.en: — They believe the tech companies represented are so powerful that they're censoring public discourse.
sentences.zh: ——他们认为所代表的科技公司如此强大，以至于正在审查公众舆论。

sentences.en: They're censoring speech.
sentences.zh: 他们在审查言论。

sentences.en: — You know, I'm concerned that the people who manage the net, and the four of you manage a big part of the net, are ending up using this as a political screen.
sentences.zh: ——你知道的，我担心管理网络的人——你们四个人管理着网络的大部分——最终会把这当作政治过滤器。

sentences.en: — I was wondering throughout that line of questioning, Cecilia, is there a case that the Republicans focusing on this idea of conservative bias kind of is related to antitrust,
sentences.zh: ——西西利亚，在整个提问过程中我一直在想，共和党人关注保守派偏见这个想法，是否与反垄断有关？

sentences.en: that ultimately these companies have a monopoly on the market of ideas?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这些公司是否垄断了观念的市场？

sentences.en: Or is this really just Republicans using this opportunity, this face time with these executives, to focus on political grievances
sentences.zh: 或者这实际上只是共和党人利用这个机会、利用与这些高管面对面的时间来关注政治怨头，

sentences.en: and kind of ignoring the intention of this hearing?
sentences.zh: 并且有点忽视了这次听证会的初衷？

sentences.en: — I do think that there's a sincere belief that antitrust is related to their concerns about censorship, because they believe that the companies have become so powerful,
sentences.zh: ——我确实认为人们真诚地相信反垄断与他们对审查制度的担忧有关，因为他们认为这些公司已经变得如此强大，

sentences.en: the social media companies, and that they are right now the biggest marketplace of ideas and the biggest exchanges of information.
sentences.zh: 这些社交媒体公司，而且它们现在是最大的观念市场和最大的信息交流中心。

sentences.en: — And so they see the problem of censorship as a symptom of companies that are too big and powerful.
sentences.zh: ——因此，他们将审查制度的问题视为公司过于庞大和强大的症状。

sentences.en: — Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: ——嗯哼。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: But we didn't really see much Republican focus on the more traditional idea of antitrust, meaning a business has gotten so big that it's hurting kind of all consumers
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有真正看到共和党人把焦点放在更传统的反垄断概念上，也就是指一家公司变得如此庞大以至于伤害了所有消费者，

sentences.en: and is anti-competitive to other businesses.
sentences.zh: 并且对其他企业具有反竞争性。

sentences.en: Is that an indication that the Republicans are less concerned about big tech as an economic threat than Democrats are?
sentences.zh: 这是否表明共和党人对作为经济威胁的大型科技公司的担忧不如民主党人那么多？

sentences.en: — Yeah, I was surprised, actually, by how little the Republican side went into the specific debates on antitrust around these companies.
sentences.zh: ——是的，事实上，共和党阵营对这些公司反垄断的具体辩论涉及得如此之少，让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: — And you did hear, for example, James Sensenbrenner, who is the ranking member of the Antitrust Subcommittee, say that—
sentences.zh: ——你确实听到，例如，反垄断小组委员会资深成员詹姆斯·森森布伦特说——

sentences.en: — I think the law is good.
sentences.zh: ——我认为法律很好。

sentences.en: — Actually, right now, the market should work itself out.
sentences.zh: ——事实上，现在市场应该自行发挥作用。

sentences.en: — And we don't need to throw it all in the wastebasket.
sentences.zh: ——我们不需要把它全部扔进垃圾桶。

sentences.en: — And that things are OK right now.
sentences.zh: ——而且目前一切都很好。

sentences.en: The laws do not need to change.
sentences.zh: 法律不需要改变。

sentences.en: — Let me ask Mr. Bezos, you know, say you were required to spin stuff off, so you might have no more of a one-stop shop.
sentences.zh: ——请允许我问贝佐斯先生，你知道的，假设你被要求拆分业务，这样你可能就不再是一个一站式商店了。

sentences.en: How are the consumers helped by that?
sentences.zh: 这对消费者有什么帮助？

sentences.en: — And said that this test, the consumer welfare standard, this test that whether prices go up
sentences.zh: ——并表示这一测试，即消费者福利标准，即价格是否上涨以及消费者选择是否减少的测试，

sentences.en: and if there are fewer options for consumers, that should remain the big test for even big tech and these tech companies.
sentences.zh: 对于大型科技公司和这些科技公司来说，这应该仍然是主要的测试标准。

sentences.en: — Sir, thank you.
sentences.zh: ——先生，谢谢你。

sentences.en: They would not be very clear.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说得很清楚。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: He said the laws don't need to change.
sentences.zh: 他说法律不需要改变。

sentences.en: — Of enforcement of those antitrust laws.
sentences.zh: ——而是对这些反垄断法的执法。

sentences.en: — But that enforcement does.
sentences.zh: ——但执法需要改变。

sentences.en: — Indeed.
sentences.zh: ——确实如此。

sentences.en: He said that enforcement is appropriate.
sentences.zh: 他说执法是恰当的。

sentences.en: The laws just simply don't need to change.
sentences.zh: 法律根本不需要改变。

sentences.en: And also, we should be careful.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们应该小心。

sentences.en: He said, in his words, he said,
sentences.zh: 他说，用他的话说，他说，

sentences.en: — Being big is not inherently bad.
sentences.zh: ——体量大并非天生就是坏事。

sentences.en: — It doesn't inherently mean that you're bad.
sentences.zh: ——这并不天然意味着你是坏人。

sentences.en: — OK, so let's talk about the most memorable exchanges involving each company when the focus
sentences.zh: ——好的，那我们来谈谈涉及每家公司的最难忘的交流，当焦点

sentences.en: was on the more traditional aspects of antitrust and the evidence that had been dug up in the course of this investigation.
sentences.zh: 放在反垄断的更传统方面以及在这次调查过程中挖掘出的证据上时。

sentences.en: Did they focus these lines of questioning on what you had predicted?
sentences.zh: 他们是否将这些提问方向集中在你预测的方面？

sentences.en: For example, Facebook, you had said, was going to be asked about its tendency to buy up competitors.
sentences.zh: 例如，关于脸书，你曾说过会被问到其收购竞争对手的倾向。

sentences.en: Is that what happened?
sentences.zh: 事实是这样的吗？

sentences.en: — I definitely expected the issue of buying up competitors to come up.
sentences.zh: ——我确实预料到收购竞争对手的问题会被提出。

sentences.en: What I did not expect is the level of specificity that was included in the line of questioning.
sentences.zh: 我没有料到的是提问中所包含的具体程度。

sentences.en: — Thank you, gentlemen.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢各位先生。

sentences.en: I now recognize the distinguished chair of the full judiciary committee,
sentences.zh: 我现在请司法委员会全体会议的杰出主席发言，

sentences.en: Mr. Nadler from New York.
sentences.zh: 来自纽约的纳德勒先生。

sentences.en: — I was really surprised, for example, that Jerry Nadler—
sentences.zh: ——我真的很惊讶，例如杰里·纳德勒——

sentences.en: — Mr. Zuckerberg, I want to thank you for providing us information during our investigation.
sentences.zh: ——扎克伯格先生，我要感谢您在我们的调查期间向我们提供信息。

sentences.en: — Brought up and read directly from emails from the top executives at Facebook during the time when they wanted to purchase Instagram.
sentences.zh: ——提出了并直接宣读了脸书高管在他们想要收购Instagram期间的电子邮件。

sentences.en: — However, the documents you provided tell a very disturbing story.
sentences.zh: ——然而，你们提供的文件讲述了一个非常令人不安的故事。

sentences.en: — And from these emails, the intent to, for example, neutralize competitors.
sentences.zh: ——从这些电子邮件中可以看出其意图，例如，消灭竞争对手。

sentences.en: — You have written that Facebook can likely always just buy any competitive startups.
sentences.zh: ——您曾写过，脸书很可能总是可以收购任何具有竞争力的初创公司。

sentences.en: — And the concern articulated in these emails.
sentences.zh: ——以及这些电子邮件中表达的担忧。

sentences.en: — When Facebook contemplated acquiring Instagram, a competitive startup, you told your CFO that though nascent, Instagram could be very disruptive to us.
sentences.zh: ——当脸书考虑收购一家具有竞争力的初创公司Instagram时，您告诉您的首席财务官，尽管Instagram尚处于萌芽期，但它对我们具有极大的颠覆性。

sentences.en: And in the weeks leading up to the deal—
sentences.zh: 就在交易达成前的几周里——

sentences.en: — That Instagram was going to be a big threat.
sentences.zh: ——Instagram将成为一个巨大的威胁。

sentences.en: — Saying that, quote, Instagram can meaningfully hurt us without becoming a huge business.
sentences.zh: ——并说，引述：“Instagram不用发展成巨型业务就能对我们造成重大伤害。”

sentences.en: — And Mark Zuckerberg responded by saying—
sentences.zh: ——马克·扎克伯格对此回应说——

sentences.en: — Yes, I've been clear that Instagram was a competitor.
sentences.zh: ——是的，我一直很明确Instagram是一个竞争对手。

sentences.en: — Well, yes, Instagram is a competitor.
sentences.zh: ——好吧，是的，Instagram是一个竞争对手。

sentences.en: And we clearly thought they were a competitor.
sentences.zh: 我们显然认为他们是一个竞争对手。

sentences.en: And by the way—
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句——

sentences.en: — I think the FTC had all of these documents and reviewed this and unanimously voted at the time not to challenge the acquisition.
sentences.zh: ——我认为联邦贸易委员会拥有所有这些文件并进行了审查，当时一致投票决定不对该收购提出异议。

sentences.en: — The FTC in 2011 approved this merger.
sentences.zh: ——联邦贸易委员会在2011年批准了这起合并。

sentences.en: So let's be clear that this has been vetted by the federal government.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要明确，这已经得到了联邦政府的审查。

sentences.en: He also said that if not for Facebook and the resources that Facebook had,
sentences.zh: 他还说，如果不是因为脸书以及脸书拥有的资源，

sentences.en: Instagram perhaps would not be the company it is today, the app that it is today, which is a wildly popular global app.
sentences.zh: Instagram也许就不会成为今天的公司，成为今天的应用程序，即一个广受欢迎的全球应用程序。

sentences.en: — And Jerry Nadler responded to that.
sentences.zh: ——杰里·纳德勒对此作出了回应。

sentences.en: — Mr. Zuckerberg, you're making my point.
sentences.zh: ——扎克伯格先生，你正合我意。

sentences.en: — I think you're proving my point.
sentences.zh: ——我认为你证明了我的观点。

sentences.en: He's saying you do take nascent competitors and you gobble them up.
sentences.zh: 他是说你确实把处于萌芽期的竞争对手吞并了。

sentences.en: And then you turn them into important parts of the Facebook ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 然后把他们变成脸书生态系统的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: But those are really interesting exchanges in particular because they were so specific.
sentences.zh: 但这些交流特别有趣，因为它们非常具体。

sentences.en: And they were taking the words of the executives in these emails and in these documents straight back to the executives and asking them directly to respond and defend themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些电子邮件和文件中的高管原话直接拿来质问高管，并要求他们直接回应和辩护。

sentences.en: And that was something that these executives aren't used to having to do and certainly not in front of the public.
sentences.zh: 这是这些高管不习惯做的事情，当然更不用说在公众面前了。

sentences.en: — Okay, let's move on to Google.
sentences.zh: ——好的，让我们继续讨论谷歌。

sentences.en: You had predicted that Google would be asked about the downside of its dominance in search.
sentences.zh: 你曾预测谷歌会被问到其在搜索领域占据主导地位的负面影响。

sentences.en: Is that what happened?
sentences.zh: 事实是这样的吗？

sentences.en: — Yes.
sentences.zh: ——是的。

sentences.en: David Cicillini asked Sundar Pichai about his search practices.
sentences.zh: 大卫·西西里尼就其搜索业务 prácticas 询问了桑达尔·皮查伊。

sentences.en: He said—
sentences.zh: 他说——

sentences.en: — We heard throughout this investigation that Google has stolen content to build your own business.
sentences.zh: ——我们在整个调查过程中听到谷歌窃取内容来建立你们自己的业务。

sentences.en: — You steal content.
sentences.zh: ——你们窃取内容。

sentences.en: You surface search results that are not necessarily the best search results, but that are the best search results for you and your services.
sentences.zh: 你们呈现的搜索结果不一定是最好的搜索结果，而是对你们和你们的服务最有利的搜索结果。

sentences.en: — These are consistent reports.
sentences.zh: ——这些是连续的报道。

sentences.en: And so your testimony that that doesn't happen is really inconsistent with what we've learned during the course of the investigation.
sentences.zh: 因此，你们声称没有发生这种情况的证词，与我们在调查过程中了解到的情况严重不符。

sentences.en: — And you steal content from companies specifically like Yelp, which is a restaurant review site.
sentences.zh: ——而且你们专门从像Yelp这样作为餐厅评论网站的公司窃取内容。

sentences.en: And you use that content to help lift and benefit other Google services.
sentences.zh: 你们利用这些内容来帮助提升和使其他谷歌服务受益。

sentences.en: David Cicillini's accusation was that Google has a walled garden of all kinds of services, and they just want users to be on their services as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 大卫·西西里尼的指控是，谷歌拥有一个包含各种服务的封闭生态系统，他们只想让用户尽可能多地留在他们的服务上。

sentences.en: And as a consequence of that, any rival is either being used or being blocked entirely from this important gateway, which is this Google search engine.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何竞争对手要么被利用，要么被完全阻挡在这个重要的门户之外，即谷歌搜索引擎。

sentences.en: — And I noticed that when the chairman tried to press the CEO of Google on, for example, this allegation of stealing content from Yelp—
sentences.zh: ——我注意到，当主席试图就例如从Yelp窃取内容的指控向谷歌首席执行官施压时——

sentences.en: — Mr. Pichai, isn't that anti-competitive?
sentences.zh: ——皮查伊先生，这难道不是反竞争的吗？

sentences.en: — The CEO of Google did not respond.
sentences.zh: ——谷歌首席执行官没有回应。

sentences.en: — Sundar Pichai, throughout his whole testimony, was very reserved.
sentences.zh: ——桑达尔·皮查伊在整个作证过程中都非常克制。

sentences.en: — Congressman, you know, when I run the company, I'm really focused on giving users what they want.
sentences.zh: ——国会议员，你知道的，当我经营这家公司时，我真的很专注于给用户他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: We conduct ourselves to the highest standard.
sentences.zh: 我们以最高标准要求自己。

sentences.en: — And often he did not reply to specific accusations.
sentences.zh: ——而且他经常没有对具体的指控做出回复。

sentences.en: And that was the case this time as well.
sentences.zh: 这次也是如此。

sentences.en: — Happy to engage, understand the specifics, and answer your questions further.
sentences.zh: ——很高兴参与，了解具体细节，并进一步回答您的提问。

sentences.en: — He was deflecting.
sentences.zh: ——他在敷衍推脱。

sentences.en: — And on Amazon, Cecilia, you had said that Jeff Bezos would be challenged about the way that company treats third-party vendors.
sentences.zh: ——至于亚马逊，西西利亚，你曾说过杰夫·贝佐斯将因公司对待第三方供应商的方式而受到质问。

sentences.en: How did that play out?
sentences.zh: 情况如何？

sentences.en: — Several lawmakers questioned Jeff Bezos about its treatment of third-party vendors.
sentences.zh: ——几位议员就亚马逊对待第三方供应商的方式质问了杰夫·贝佐斯。

sentences.en: — Does Amazon ever access and use third-party seller data when making business decisions?
sentences.zh: ——亚马逊在做出商业决策时是否曾访问和使用第三方卖家数据？

sentences.en: And just a yes or no will suffice, sir?
sentences.zh: 先生，只要回答是或不是就足够了？

sentences.en: — I can't answer that question, yes or no.
sentences.zh: ——我无法用是或不是来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: — Representative Lucy McBeth.
sentences.zh: ——众议员露西·麦克巴斯。

sentences.en: — And we've interviewed many small businesses, and they use the words like bullying, fear, and panic to describe their relationship with Amazon.
sentences.zh: ——我们采访了许多小企业，他们用欺凌、恐惧和恐慌等词来形容他们与亚马逊的关系。

sentences.en: — Aired the recording from one of her constituents in her district, who was a bookseller on Amazon.
sentences.zh: ——播放了她选区中一位选民的录音，该选民是亚马逊上的一名书商。

sentences.en: — And as we grew, we were shrinking Amazon's market share in the textbooks category.
sentences.zh: ——随着我们的成长，我们缩小了亚马逊在教科书品类的市场份额。

sentences.en: — And this bookseller was delisted from the marketplace.
sentences.zh: ——而这位书商被市场除名了。

sentences.en: — So now we're in retaliation, Amazon started restricting us from selling.
sentences.zh: ——所以现在我们遭到报复，亚马逊开始限制我们销售。

sentences.en: — And in this recording, we heard the bookseller talk about how being delisted essentially crippled her business entirely.
sentences.zh: ——在这段录音中，我们听到书商谈到被除名是如何从根本上彻底瘫痪了她的生意的。

sentences.en: — We haven't sold a single book from the past 10 months.
sentences.zh: — 我们过去10个月连一本书都没卖出去。

sentences.en: We were never given a reason.
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有得到过任何理由。

sentences.en: Amazon didn't even provide us with a notice as to why we were being restricted.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊甚至没有给我们发任何通知，解释我们为什么受到限制。

sentences.en: There was no warning.
sentences.zh: 没有任何警告。

sentences.en: There was no plan.
sentences.zh: 没有任何计划。

sentences.en: — What did that anecdote, that audio tape, illustrate about Amazon and this question of antitrust?
sentences.zh: — 那段轶事、那段录音，说明了亚马逊和反垄断问题之间的什么情况？

sentences.en: — I think it demonstrated that Amazon is so big.
sentences.zh: — 我认为这表明亚马逊体量太大了。

sentences.en: — Do you think this is an acceptable way to treat someone that you described as both a partner and a customer?
sentences.zh: — 你认为这是对待一个你既描述为合作伙伴又描述为客户的人的应有方式吗？

sentences.en: — And it spoke to the fact that Amazon, in a way, has become its own economy.
sentences.zh: — 这说明亚马逊在某种程度上已经成为了它自己的经济体。

sentences.en: — No, Congresswoman, and I appreciate you showing me that anecdote.
sentences.zh: — 不，国会女议员，我很感谢你向我展示那段轶事。

sentences.en: — You could say the same thing with Apple, too, in its App Store.
sentences.zh: — 关于苹果及其应用商店，你也可以这么说。

sentences.en: There's so many other companies that depend on these economies and platforms, if you will, for their livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 有那么多其他公司依靠这些经济体和平台（如果你愿意这么叫的话）来维持生计。

sentences.en: And in a way, they've become their own sub-economies, all four of them, actually.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它们实际上都成了各自的子经济体，所有这四家公司都是如此。

sentences.en: — You just mentioned Apple.
sentences.zh: — 你刚刚提到了苹果。

sentences.en: And it was your prediction that this hearing would be about the App Store and not much else.
sentences.zh: 你的预测是，这次听证会将围绕应用商店展开，除此之外没有别的。

sentences.en: Was that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样的吗？

sentences.en: — That was the case.
sentences.zh: — 确实如此。

sentences.en: With Apple, Tim Cook was asked about Apple's control.
sentences.zh: 在苹果公司，蒂姆·库克被问及苹果的控制权。

sentences.en: — Over its App Store.
sentences.zh: — 对其应用商店的控制。

sentences.en: And Representative Hank Johnson, a Democrat from Georgia, asked Tim Cook.
sentences.zh: 来自佐治亚州的民主党众议员汉克·约翰逊问蒂姆·库克：

sentences.en: — Mr. Cook, does Apple not treat all app developers equally?
sentences.zh: — 库克先生，苹果难道没有平等对待所有应用开发者吗？

sentences.en: — If he treated all apps fairly.
sentences.zh: — 如果他公平对待所有应用的话。

sentences.en: He asked, why is it that developers have to get permission?
sentences.zh: 他问，为什么开发者必须获得许可？

sentences.en: And why is it that you charge developers 30% commission, on average, for simply operating on iPhones?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们向开发者收取平均30%的佣金，仅仅因为他们在iPhone上运营？

sentences.en: — If you look back at history—
sentences.zh: — 如果你回顾历史——

sentences.en: — What's to stop Apple from increasing its commission to 50%?
sentences.zh: — 是什么阻止苹果将佣金提高到50%？

sentences.en: — Sir, we have never increased commissions in the store since the first day it operated in 2008.
sentences.zh: — 先生，自2008年应用商店开业第一天起，我们从未提高过佣金。

sentences.en: — There's nothing to stop you from doing so, is it?
sentences.zh: — 没有什么能阻止你这么做，不是吗？

sentences.en: — What's to stop you from raising that commission price?
sentences.zh: — 是什么阻止你提高佣金价格？

sentences.en: The line of questioning really was about how Apple maintains its monopoly over that App Store
sentences.zh: 这一连串的提问实际上是关于苹果如何保持其对该应用商店的垄断

sentences.en: and makes sure that it stays ahead of rivals by that dominant gateway position that they have as the controller of the App Store.
sentences.zh: 并通过其作为应用商店控制者的主导网关地位，确保自己始终领先于竞争对手。

sentences.en: — So we had fierce competition at the developer side and the customer side, which is essentially, it's so competitive,
sentences.zh: — 所以我们在开发者端和客户端都有激烈的竞争，从本质上讲，竞争非常激烈，

sentences.en: I would describe it as a street fight for market share in the smartphone business.
sentences.zh: 我称之为争夺智能手机业务市场份额的街头斗殴。

sentences.en: — And Tim Cook really didn't have a great answer.
sentences.zh: — 蒂姆·库克确实没有给出很好的回答。

sentences.en: — As a great American Supreme Court Justice Lewis Brandeis once said, we must make our choice.
sentences.zh: — 正如伟大的美国最高法院大法官路易斯·布兰代斯曾经说过的那样，我们必须做出选择。

sentences.en: We may have democracy, or we may have wealth concentrated in the hands of a few, but we can't have both.
sentences.zh: 我们可以拥有民主，或者我们可以将财富集中在少数人手中，但我们两者兼得。

sentences.en: This concludes today's hearing.
sentences.zh: 今天的听证会到此结束。

sentences.en: Without objection, this hearing is adjourned.
sentences.zh: 如无异议，本听证会休会。

sentences.en: — So let's talk about how this all went.
sentences.zh: — 那么我们来谈谈这一切的进展情况。

sentences.en: This was supposed to be big techs, big tobacco moment, as you said.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这本该是科技界的“大烟草”时刻。

sentences.en: But Democrats and Republicans were up to two very different things in this hearing.
sentences.zh: 但在这次听证会上，民主党人和共和党人有着截然不同的目的。

sentences.en: And I'm mindful that lawmakers have been ridiculed in the past for their kind of shallow understanding of technology in hearings like this.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，过去立法者在类似的听证会上因对技术的浅薄理解而遭到嘲笑。

sentences.en: And this is for tech companies that are distinctly difficult to understand because of their vastness, you know, pinning down their inner workings.
sentences.zh: 这是因为科技公司由于规模庞大而极其难以理解，你知道的，很难摸清它们的内部运作机制。

sentences.en: And so I'm wondering if you think that this did feel like a big tobacco moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是否觉得这真的有大烟草时刻的感觉。

sentences.en: Did this hearing accomplish what lawmakers had intended?
sentences.zh: 这次听证会达到了立法者的预期吗？

sentences.en: — This hearing felt like big techs, big tobacco moment, in that for the first time, the four CEOs of the four biggest technology companies
sentences.zh: — 这场听证会确实有科技界的“大烟草”时刻的感觉，因为四家最大科技公司的四位CEO有史以来第一次

sentences.en: had to defend themselves from accusations that were pretty tough, that presented these companies in a pretty dark and negative light
sentences.zh: 不得不为一些相当严厉的指控进行辩护，这些指控将这些公司置于一个非常黑暗和负面的光芒中，

sentences.en: as brutal, dominant enterprises that are willing to squash competition and harm consumers along the way to maintain their dominance.
sentences.zh: 把它们描绘成残酷、占据主导地位的企业，为了维持其主导地位，不惜打压竞争对手并损害消费者利益。

sentences.en: In that way, the hearing presented them through a lens that the companies had not before been viewed through by consumers or the public.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，听证会以一种消费者或公众以前从未有过的视角展现了这些公司。

sentences.en: The hearing really presented the companies as something different than just tech startups.
sentences.zh: 听证会确实将这些公司展现为不仅仅是科技初创企业。

sentences.en: They presented them as big enterprises, very similar to the trusts of the late 1800s and the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 它们被展现为大型企业，非常类似于19世纪末和20世纪初的托拉斯。

sentences.en: — At that time, the same sort of debates were swirling around whether it was good for U.S.
sentences.zh: — 当时，围绕着美国钢铁公司或标准石油公司成为如此庞大的企业、成为如此大的参与者并拥有如此大的影响力究竟是否是件好事，

sentences.en: steel or for Standard Oil to be such sprawling enterprises and to be such big actors and have so much influence.
sentences.zh: 也曾充斥着同样的争论。

sentences.en: — So where does this leave us now?
sentences.zh: — 那么这让我们现在处于什么位置？

sentences.en: I mean, this culmination of a 13-month investigation, this spectacle of this hearing, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一项历时13个月调查的高潮，是这场听证会的奇观，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: — So that's a big question, Michael.
sentences.zh: — 这是一个很大的问题，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I think that what you saw was agreement among the Republicans and Democrats that they were angry at these technology companies and they had a lot of concerns.
sentences.zh: 我认为你看到的是共和党人和民主党人达成了一致，他们对这些科技公司感到愤怒，并且有很多担忧。

sentences.en: But where you're going to see disagreement is what comes next in terms of legislative change,
sentences.zh: 但你会看到分歧的地方在于，接下来在立法变革方面会发生什么，

sentences.en: what comes next also in terms of recommendations to enforcement agencies that are actually investigating these companies at this time.
sentences.zh: 接下来在对目前正在调查这些公司的执法机构的建议方面会发生什么。

sentences.en: So there's going to be a lot of disagreement as to the path forward is going ahead.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于未来的发展道路，将会存在很多分歧。

sentences.en: What does change is that these companies now really can't shake this image that they have an antitrust problem,
sentences.zh: 所改变的是，这些公司现在真的无法摆脱这种形象：它们存在反垄断问题，

sentences.en: that all of them are in some way dominant and have abused their monopoly power to harm competition and potentially to harm consumers as well.
sentences.zh: 它们都在某种程度上占据主导地位，并滥用了其垄断权力来损害竞争，并可能也损害消费者利益。

sentences.en: And that's not the kind of tag that any of these companies want attached to them.
sentences.zh: 这不是任何这些公司都希望贴上的标签。

sentences.en: — In other words, once you have been tagged as a trust and a monopoly, it's probably just a question of what the regulatory answer to that is.
sentences.zh: — 换句话说，一旦你被贴上了托拉斯和垄断的标签，这可能就只是一个监管应对措施是什么的问题了。

sentences.en: — Yeah, I think it's just a question of time.
sentences.zh: — 是的，我认为这只是时间问题。

sentences.en: — Thank you, Cecilia.
sentences.zh: — 谢谢你，塞西莉亚。

sentences.en: — Thank you.
sentences.zh: — 谢谢。

sentences.en: — We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: — 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: — The Times reports that more than 150,000 people have died from the coronavirus in the U.S., a new milestone in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: — 《纽约时报》报道称，已有超过15万人在美国死于冠状病毒，这是大流行中的一个新里程碑。

sentences.en: The death rate, which had briefly fallen over the summer, is now rising in 23 different states, especially in Arizona, South Carolina, and Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 死亡率在夏天曾短暂下降，现在正在23个不同的州上升，尤其是在南卡罗来纳州、密西西比州和亚利桑那州。

sentences.en: — On average, the virus has killed 1,000 people a day over the past week alone.
sentences.zh: — 仅在过去一周，该病毒平均每天夺走1000人的生命。

sentences.en: And the governor of Oregon, Kate Brown, said that federal officers would begin to withdraw from the city of Portland today.
sentences.zh: 俄勒冈州州长凯特·布朗表示，联邦官员将于今天开始撤出波特兰市。

sentences.en: — Under an agreement between the governor and the Trump administration, Oregon State Police will provide security for the exterior of the city's federal courthouse,
sentences.zh: — 根据州长和特朗普政府之间的一项协议，俄勒冈州州警将为该市联邦法院的外部提供安全保障，

sentences.en: replacing the federal officers who had repeatedly clashed with and tear-gassed protesters there.
sentences.zh: 取代了先前在那里与抗议者发生多次冲突并向其发射催泪瓦斯的联邦官员。

sentences.en: — You hear all sorts of reports about us leaving.
sentences.zh: — 你听到各种关于我们要离开的报道。

sentences.en: We're not leaving until they've secured their city.
sentences.zh: 在他们确保城市安全之前，我们不会离开。

sentences.en: We told the governor, we told the mayor, secure your city.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉了州长，我们告诉了市长，确保你们城市的安全。

sentences.en: — Even as the negotiations to leave were underway,
sentences.zh: — 尽管撤离谈判正在进行中，

sentences.en: President Trump threatened that federal agents would remain in Portland or return there.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统仍威胁称，联邦特工将继续留在波特兰或重返该地。

sentences.en: — If they don't secure their city soon, we have no choice.
sentences.zh: — 如果他们不尽快确保城市安全，我们将别无选择。

sentences.en: We're going to have to go in and clean it out.
sentences.zh: 我们将不得不进去清理它。

sentences.en: We'll do it very easily.
sentences.zh: 我们会非常轻松地做到这一点。

sentences.en: We're all prepared to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们都准备好这样做了。

sentences.en: — So in Portland, they have to clean out their city.
sentences.zh: — 所以在波特兰，他们必须清理他们的城市。

sentences.en: — That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: — 《每日新闻》就到这里。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: — 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: — When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: — 当选举迎来了群自称改革派的人时。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。
